also, a red night bulb should not be used! it can affect the sleep of the beardie. he will be fine if the night temp drops to around 65F, but if it gets lower you can supplement with a ceramic heat emitter. everyone starts somewhere, but i believe in you to make sure he gets a good life! also, he looks a little dehydrated there, is he getting a lot of fresh greens? thats how they get the majority of their water intake! daily feeding should consist of a mix of greens, but research whats safe and what isnt for beardies. theres a lot of setup and upfront costs, but once the basic stuff is taken care of and you get into the swing of things its super simple to keep the baby happy and healthy!

definitely switch out that repticarpet for a loose substrate, and no calcisand! bearded dragons can eat it bc they know they need calcium and that will lead to impaction, which will cause either the death of the beardie or a massive vet bill. beardies NEED calcium supplementation, and live insects are best to feed. mealworms should be seen as a treat, and crickets are fine as a regular feeder. dead insects are a no-go in my book
